issues.title: Disprove conjecture 00000000145 as stated: alpha = 1/2 removes positive LIL fluctuations
issues.body:
The statement, as written, does not require alpha to be irrational. Taking alpha = 1/2 and f(x) = cos(2πx) gives mean zero. Every odd prime contributes -1 and p = 2 contributes +1, so the centered sum is exactly 2 - π(x) for x ≥ 2. Since π(x) tends to infinity, this is eventually negative, so it cannot have the positive fluctuations required by the asserted two-sided Ω± bound.

The Lean project verifies the arithmetic core that all primes greater than 2 are odd. The report gives the trigonometric and asymptotic steps explicitly and notes that an intended irrationality hypothesis is missing.

scope: Literal unrestricted alpha only; source lacks irrational or a.e. premise. Actual smooth periodic sine, real interval mean, genuine prime cutoff/fract sum, exact LIL scale and cofinal Omega signs. No claim against irrational/a.e. versions.
